thread.title: New Highs: These 4 Stocks Rally; 3 Come From This Sector

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: New Highs: These 4 Stocks Rally; 3 Come From This Sector
text:
Pfizer ( PFE ), Merck ( MRK ) and Aetna ( AET ) on Friday helped lead a small yet growing group of large- and megacap stocks rising to new highs and expanding gains past proper buy points .
X Both Pfizer and Merck, two of the 30 components in the Dow Jones industrial average, reeled off weekly gains of 2% to 4% through Friday afternoon. The former cleared the 39.43 left-side high of a six-month saucer base on July 31, which followed another long saucer pattern .
Taking 39.53 as a buy point, or 10 cents above the base's high, Pfizer has now rallied more than 6%. It's best to pick up shares when they are within the 5% buy zone . Pfizer arguably offered an early breakout at 36.90 on July 5, when shares rallied past a tightly drawn handle. The high of that three-week handle was 36.80.
Pfizer Hits New Highs On Rising Profits Earnings at the giant in treatments for epilepsy, neuralgia, arthritis and high cholesterol have grown 5%, 10%, 32%, 12% and 21% in the past five quarters. Sales in Q2 rose 4%. Wall Street sees full-year profit growing 13% to $2.99 a share, a faster rate than its three- and five-year growth rates.
Pfizer has 5.85 billion shares outstanding and a market value of $246 billion, less than a quarter of the $1 trillion market cap of Apple ( AAPL ). Pfizer's annualized dividend yield is 3.3%.
Merck (market cap of $183 billion, 2.8% yield) reached as high as 69.23, padding its gain from a breakout past a saucer base at 66.51 to 4%. In other words, the ethical drug giant remains in buy range. The stock has a mediocre EPS Rating of 60, but profits have risen for five quarters in a row. Growth has averaged 8% over that time. The Street sees full-year earnings up 9% to $4.28 a share this year and up 7% in 2019.
Health Insurers Rising To New Highs Aetna ($65 billion, 1% yield) has rolled past a 191.60 handle buy point in its long saucer and remains in buy range . The managed health care plan giant's full-year profit is seen rising 14% in 2018 to $11.24 a share.
Waste Management ( WM ) ($39 billion) cleared an 89.83 saucer entry on July 30 and hit a new high of 91.40 Friday. Shares remain within the 5% buy zone . It boasts a decent 88 EPS Rating. The waste collection and recycling titan is on track to boost earnings by 26% to $4.06 a share in 2018. Profits have grown for 18 quarters in a row, according to data from William O'Neil + Co., an IBD sister firm.
